solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boots may occupy this tiny building

definitions.meaning: a cardboard carton that a new pair of boots comes in
informally, a cramped little house or room is called by this name

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint that a pair of boots could move into some minuscule structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the carton footwear is sold in, and a slang term for a cramped dwelling.

clue.text: Judge right to cut a little fee

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is made to cut into the phrase for a little, splitting it

parts.note: a little means a bit
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Someone resolving a dispute by trimming a small charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' reads as trimming the fee, but it is the instruction to push the letter for right into the phrase meaning a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to decide a dispute as an impartial referee, so it works as the verb judge.

clue.text: In France I will meet businessman, a Roman Catholic

parts.note: je is the French word for I
a suit is slang for a businessman in formal clothes

explanation.surface: A French-set meeting with an executive who turns out to be a Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Society of Jesus is a Roman Catholic priest or brother of that order.

clue.text: We copied guards playing with guns

indicators.note: the word for copied surrounds, as if guarding, the word for playing

parts.note: aped means copied or imitated
on means playing, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: Children imitating sentries in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' looks like a noun for sentries; here it is a verb, the word for copied enclosing the word for playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furnished with arms is to be equipped with guns, an old adjective for an armed party.

clue.text: Expert put away a rake? No

definitions.note: a rake is a very thin person; the definition describes someone who is not thin

parts.note: well up in a subject means expert or knowledgeable in it
a pistol put away is holstered

explanation.surface: Someone who skilfully stows a garden rake, denying it is one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' here is a skinny person, not a libertine or garden tool; the definition is the denial, someone plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorously, a person with plenty of padding is plump, the opposite of a beanpole-thin figure.

clue.text: Clay and wicker houses top for tourism in Spanish resort

parts.note: Cassius Clay became Muhammad Ali

indicators.note: the word for wicker contains, as a house does, the letter taken from tourism

parts.note: cane is the material of wickerwork

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, here of tourism

explanation.surface: Building materials and holiday trade in a Spanish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clay' is the boxer, not the material; 'houses' puts T, the first letter of 'tourism' ('top for'), inside CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Costa Blanca is a well-known Spanish holiday resort.

clue.text: 200 parts of us are found

indicators.note: the numeral separates the letters of the word for of us, parting it

parts.note: our means belonging to us, of us
CC is 200 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A statement that two hundred pieces of us exist somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun, pieces of us; it is a verb, the numeral splitting the word for of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that occur exist or turn up, as in 'such errors occur often'.

clue.text: Strange things one has to cross — great bridges to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upward, so the whole string is reversed
the word for great spans the other letters, enclosing them as a bridge spans a gap

parts.note: ace means great or excellent
I is the Roman numeral one
has to is read as to, the letters taken as written
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A traveller facing a river with fine bridges leading northward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridges' is a verb of containment and 'to the north' turns the whole result upward, as a down clue reads; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are curious items from foreign places, odd and unfamiliar objects.

clue.text: Ask for clean house and empty garage

parts.note: to char is to work as a cleaner in houses

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters, here of garage

explanation.surface: A list of domestic chores: tidy the home, clear out the garage.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge for something is to ask a price for it, so the phrase works as demanding payment.

clue.text: Runner admitting part of foot is cut

indicators.note: the word for runner lets in the measurement, containing it

parts.note: a runner can be a loop or ring through which something runs
an inch is a twelfth of a foot

explanation.surface: An athlete with a foot injury who has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' and 'foot' suggest an athlete's injury; the foot is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut in the butchery sense is a piece of meat, and this is one taken from the loin.

clue.text: Cars I'm unsure about left unused

indicators.note: about signals turning round the cars and the hesitation together

parts.note: Audis are German cars
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: A motorist hesitating over which cars to leave unused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns round the German cars and the hesitation together; 'left' is the abbreviation, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A residual amount is what remains after the rest is consumed, the part not used up.

clue.text: Pair opening and filling sack with butterflies

indicators.note: the openings of a pair of words, the first letters of and and filling

parts.note: to sack a town is to raid and plunder it

explanation.surface: A lepidopterist opening a bag and stuffing it with butterflies.
explanation.definitionFit: Having butterflies in your stomach means being nervous, so frightened fits the idiom.

clue.text: Prepare poster for distribution and go canvassing

parts.note: to do a dish or room is to prepare it

indicators.note: letters set out for distribution are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Election instructions: get a poster ready for handing out and go canvassing.
explanation.definitionFit: To doorstep is to call at houses, as a campaigner does when canvassing votes.

clue.text: Hotel enclosure including its collection of offers?

indicators.note: the two-part outer string takes in the given letters

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a quad is an enclosed courtyard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel courtyard packed with sale offers.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'offer' here is one who offs, slang for killing, so the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of assassins is a band of killers, people who off others.

clue.text: Tender words apt to be repeated

definitions.meaning: a tender is a formal price offer, a quote
a well-known saying cited by others is passage that people repeat

explanation.surface: Kind remarks that people tend to say again.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a builder's price estimate, and a line cited from a writer.

clue.text: Soldier, name's the same

parts.note: the punctuation mark after Soldier is a comma
do is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: A soldier insisting his name is identical to someone else's.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma printed in the clue supplies its own name as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier in an elite raiding unit.

clue.text: This country house, miles off, with nothing in it

indicators.note: the round zero is put inside the rearranged letters
off here means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A country house standing some miles off with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the rearrangement and 'in it' places the zero within it; 'This country' is the definition, not part of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: One's native land is where one belongs, so this country from a resident's view.

clue.text: Vacation curtailed — awful tragedy

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so the remaining letters are jumbled
a curtailed word has lost its tail, its final letter

explanation.surface: A holiday cut short is an awful tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the last letter of 'Vacation' and 'awful' rearranges VACATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavia is a Roman play about Nero's wife, traditionally attributed to Seneca, a tragedy.

clue.text: Poet's dead — letter read out by Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: gone means dead
the letter J spelt as it is said

explanation.surface: An announcement of a poet's death read out by the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of GONE JAY to hear the name of the author of The Beggar's Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of The Beggar's Opera was an eighteenth-century English poet and dramatist.

clue.text: Perfect condition — fluffy and moist

indicators.note: fluffy means soft and loosened, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cake described as being in ideal shape: light and moist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one of the holy is a state of sanctity, a condition of moral perfection.

clue.text: Sort of at home and not at home

parts.note: in means at home
away means not at home

explanation.surface: A paradox about being both present and absent at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning partly or to some extent, as in 'it was a relief'.

clue.text: A semi-victorious court

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the word for victorious is used

parts.note: triumphant means victorious

explanation.surface: A tennis court where play was half-won.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a central open courtyard or hall within a building.

clue.text: Island area that supports one game

indicators.note: in a down clue the area letter sits beneath, supporting the rest

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals
biz is short for business, as in the game or line of trade

explanation.surface: A district that backs a particular sport.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Spain's Balearic Islands, a Mediterranean holiday destination.

clue.text: Tough old deputy

parts.note: ex means former, old
an acting official deputises for another

explanation.surface: A hard-bitten veteran second-in-command.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding and severe, a tough standard.

clue.text: Those introducing The Voice divulge secret recipe for viewer

indicators.note: the introducing letters of the three words that follow

parts.note: inner means private or secret, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: Talent-show contestants revealing a secret recipe to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The Voice is a TV singing contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready meal eaten in front of the television is food designed for a viewer.

clue.text: Batty kid's first to chase a nerdy type

indicators.note: chase means follow, so the other pieces come after the A

parts.note: Nora Batty is a character in the British TV sitcom Last of the Summer Wine

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of kid

explanation.surface: A mad youngster pursuing someone geeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like mad, but is the surname of Nora Batty from British TV comedy Last of the Summer Wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, after the waterproof jacket trainspotters wear.

clue.text: Detective facing a charge turned suspicious

indicators.note: turned signals the whole string read backwards

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector
on means facing, as in on the charge
a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: An officer confronted with an accusation becomes wary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being paranoid means being unreasonably distrustful, so suspicious is a fair synonym.
